title: Architecture as Evidence: Reading the Built Environment Through Forensic Investigation
text:
Architecture as Evidence: Reading the Built Environment Through Forensic Investigation

Architecture is commonly examined through its visible form, materials and spatial organisation. The physical fabric of a building can also retain evidence of events and alterations that are not apparent from its present appearance. Cracks, repairs and structural changes may indicate when and how a building was modified, while photographs and material fragments can provide further evidence about the circumstances surrounding those changes. Forensic investigation examines these traces, using the built environment and its surrounding records to establish how particular events, alterations or failures occurred.

title: Lisbon Architecture Triennale Announces CO-OP as Theme for Its 2028 Edition
text:
Lisbon Architecture Triennale Announces CO-OP as Theme for Its 2028 Edition

The 8th Lisbon Architecture Triennale has announced CO-OP as the title of its 2028 edition, which will explore cooperation and its relationship with architecture, housing, production, and collective forms of living. Led by Chief Curator Joaquim Moreno, the upcoming edition will examine how cooperation can inform alternative ways of producing, building, and inhabiting spaces, while addressing questions of ownership, governance, and the common good. The Triennale will open on September 28, 2028, with a free three-day programme running through September 30 in Lisbon, Portugal.

title: Connecting Architectural Education with Specialized Fields at SCI-Arc
text:
Connecting Architectural Education with Specialized Fields at SCI-Arc

Artificial intelligence, climate challenges, and new media are changing how architects work and the knowledge they draw on. These shifts also raise questions about architectural education and how professional training can connect with specialized fields. SCI-Arc's new Accelerated Master of Science pathway offers one approach, allowing students to combine a professional architecture degree with a postgraduate degree in artificial intelligence, ecological design, media, or architectural pedagogy through one additional year of study.

title: Mecanoo Appointed to Transform Zutphen's Theatre Hanzehof into a New Cultural Center in the Netherlands
text:
Mecanoo Appointed to Transform Zutphen's Theatre Hanzehof into a New Cultural Center in the Netherlands

Following a European tender procedure, the Municipality of Zutphen, Netherlands, has appointed Mecanoo to transform the existing Theatre Hanzehof & Buitensociëteit into a cultural destination. The project, called Hanzehuis, was developed in collaboration with Hanzehof theater, de Muzehof center for the arts, and BIJ de Bieb library, and with ABT Consulting engineers and building services consultant Nelissen. It involves designing a new center for culture, knowledge and exchange, preserving the main historic building and introducing a new volume to accommodate cultural activities, education and community life under a single roof. Mecanoo contributed to the preparatory phase, and this appointment marks the transition to developing the design further with the professional team, the Municipality and the participating cultural organizations.

title: World Building of The Year and Interior of The Year revealed at World Architecture Festival 2026
text:
World Building of The Year and Interior of The Year revealed at World Architecture Festival 2026

The Prestige University by Sanjay Puri Architects in Indore, India, has been declared the World Building of the Year at the 2026 World Architecture Festival (WAF). The ultimate accolades of World Building of the Year, World Interior of the Year, and Future Project of the Year were announced as hundreds of architects from across the world convened at a grand finale Gala Dinner at the Broward County Convention Center in Florida. A host of Special Prizes, including the American Beauty Prize sponsored by RFACT, were also announced at the closing event to celebrate the nineteenth edition of the festival. The announcement follows the final day of WAF, in which prize winners across all 42 categories have been competing for the winning titles.

title: Holding Light: The Bahá’í Temple of South America in Santiago, Chile
text:
Holding Light: The Bahá’í Temple of South America in Santiago, Chile

Santiago spreads across the valley floor, and above its eastern edge, where the streets of Peñalolén give way to the foothills of the Andes, a pale form rises from a carved terrace: nine curved wings leaning toward one another. At dawn the building takes on the cold blue of the cordillera behind it. By midday it is a tent of white light, by late afternoon it turns gold, and after dark the sequence reverses: the temple becomes a lantern.

title: Powerhouse Parramatta / Moreau Kusunoki + Genton
text:
Powerhouse Parramatta / Moreau Kusunoki + Genton

Funded by the NSW Government and located on Dharug land, Powerhouse Parramatta is a major new landmark for Australia, making Western Sydney a global cultural destination. Its opening marks the most significant cultural infrastructure project since the Sydney Opera House. Powerhouse Parramatta, combined with the relocation of the Collection to Castle Hill, is a $A915 million project, including $A75 million in philanthropic contributions.

title: Yokohama Timber Wharf / Taiju Yamashita Design and Architecture
text:
Yokohama Timber Wharf / Taiju Yamashita Design and Architecture

Set in Rinko Park, the largest green space in Yokohama's Minato Mirai 21 district, Yokohama Timber Wharf is a multipurpose facility designed to connect architecture with the life of the waterfront park. Facing Yokohama Bay, the park's seaside promenade and broad lawns attract families, runners, and visitors throughout the year. The project brings dining and outdoor recreation support into this setting, creating a new gathering place and encouraging movement through Yokohama's coastal city center. DRAFT leads the development, while Taiju Yamashita Design and Architecture is responsible for the architectural design.

title: Why Material Lifespan Matters More Than Ever
text:
Why Material Lifespan Matters More Than Ever

A material's environmental footprint cannot be fully understood without considering its lifespan. A product with relatively low embodied carbon may require frequent replacement, additional installation resources, and repeated disposal over the life of a building. Conversely, a material with a higher initial impact may offer greater long-term value through its durability, reducing the need for future interventions. From this perspective, longevity goes beyond being a technical characteristic; it becomes an essential component of responsible architectural design.

title: Shoe Factory Gatehouses / Xie Jie Architects
text:
Shoe Factory Gatehouses / Xie Jie Architects

A new shoe factory complex in Wenzhou is about to open, but two gatehouses at its south entrance remain unfinished. Through the existing frames, one sees the West Yandang Mountains and a silver metal warehouse at their foot, diagonally across the entrance. The client wished to retain the frames to maintain continuity with the complex, while giving the entrance a distinct character of its own.

This commercial building stands on a corner at an intersection along Komazawa Park Avenue. With cars, bicycles, and pedestrians passing by, the design considers how a building can respond to a major road through a neighbourhood of educational and medical institutions. Its materials and composition seek to balance sensitivity to the surroundings with a distinct presence.

title: M-House / Country House. Architecture
text:
M-House / Country House. Architecture

Amid a quiet neighborhood in Phan Thiet, where the sun warms the walls and sea breezes weave their way beneath tiled roofs, M-House emerges with an understated charm. On a modest plot surrounded by neighboring homes on three sides, we chose an open architectural configuration to bring natural light, fresh air, and greenery into everyday life.

title: Casa Amigó / Estudio Travertino
text:
Casa Amigó / Estudio Travertino

Some renovations update spaces; others reorganize how they are lived in. Casa Amigó belongs to the second group. Located in Barcelona's Sant Gervasi-Galvany neighborhood, this 1970s family home starts with a clear idea: to change how the space is perceived and inhabited. The project turns the flat into an interior landscape where color, material, and light reorganize the relationships between rooms.

title: Rosaleda Terrace / RH-EL
text:
Rosaleda Terrace / RH-EL

Behind a discreet fence in a residence located in Villahermosa city of Tabasco. You can find a majestic garden hidden. The property has the fortune to be situated on the shores of the iconic Illusions Lagoon, where you can see part of Tabasco’s faun, like morelet’s crocodiles, pejelagartos, manatees and some birds from the region.

title: Sede Ser Headquarters / Atelier 77
text:
Sede Ser Headquarters / Atelier 77

The expansion of the Ser Cidadão Headquarters in Santa Cruz, the west zone of Rio de Janeiro, embodies in architecture the commitment of a social organization to human and community development. Since 2002, the organization has been involved in projects related to education, culture, work, and health, promoting opportunities for youth in vulnerable territories. In 2006, it received a donation of a historic mansion, the former residence of doctor and senator Júlio Cesário de Melo, whose legacy of care inspired the very essence of the project: to build spaces that welcome, educate, and transform.

title: LDN House / ERENTIA
text:
LDN House / ERENTIA

In LDN, ERENTIA transforms an existing London residence into a home for two: two people who share a life, but not necessarily all of their daily needs. The project rethinks domestic structure through varying degrees of proximity, creating spaces that allow the couple to gather, share, and find distance when needed. Two people, one house, two workspaces. One bathroom, two sinks, two showers. Autonomy, parallels, and distance.

title: AUA Najarian Center / Storaket Architectural Studio
text:
AUA Najarian Center / Storaket Architectural Studio

The Najarian Center is a key facility of the American University of Armenia (AUA), located in Yerevan, near the Sergei Parajanov Museum. Established with the support of K. George and Dr. Carolann Najarian, the center is part of a broader initiative to drive social change in Armenia through education and innovation. It provides spaces and resources for learning, collaboration, and fostering social entrepreneurship. As part of the project, reconstruction work has been carried out on the building, including seismic retrofitting, interior and exterior renovations, and the comprehensive implementation of engineering systems.

title: Modern and Mexican: Mario Pani’s CUPA Housing Complex in Mexico City
text:
Modern and Mexican: Mario Pani’s CUPA Housing Complex in Mexico City

In 1947, Mexico's General Directorate of Civil Pensions commissioned young architect Mario Pani to design 200 houses for government employees on a recently acquired plot of land in Colonia del Valle, then a distant neighborhood on the outskirts of Mexico City. Rather than following the original guidelines, Pani proposed a 13-story housing complex with extensive green areas, communal spaces, and more than a thousand apartments. Drawing on Le Corbusier's functionalist principles, the architect created a project that opened in 1949 and would become a landmark in Latin American modern architecture.

title: ATO RAMEN / CUDO:
text:
ATO RAMEN / CUDO:

The starting point for ATO Ramen in Warsaw was the idea of making the ramen-making process an essential part of the guest experience. Rather than hiding food preparation behind closed doors, we designed an open kitchen and a glazed noodle production area as the heart of the restaurant.

title: Strata House / VPA Architects
text:
Strata House / VPA Architects

Strata House is a project rooted in quiet and calming living. The house was curated around a singular conviction — designing around the climate to make light and shadows its most eloquent architectural gesture. The south-facing plot demanded a pronounced response. Deep overhead projections extend across the façade to intercept the sun before it reaches the open glass beneath. The built mass stretches further towards the west to cast shade over the garden and veranda below, extending the architecture itself into a landscape of comfort. These sleek floating slabs are functional at their core, yet visually, they give the elevation a unique identity: a composition of strong horizontals and quiet repose. On the exterior, a locally quarried and fine-grained Gwalior Mint sandstone wraps the building with a characteristic green-grey luminosity, carrying the memory of its region with a material honesty.

title: Police Station for the People / STUDIO MOTLEY
text:
Police Station for the People / STUDIO MOTLEY

"Build us a Police Station that people don't find intimidating." This simple, yet unusually perceptive brief from the Additional Commissioner became the starting point for rethinking the conventional police station. Located in Devanahalli, a town on the outskirts of Bangalore with a history spanning over 500 years, the project offered an opportunity to reconsider not just the architecture of a largely neglected building typology, but also the relationship between a public institution and the people it serves.

title: Biarritz Building - Cooperative Housing / Ariel Jacubovich | Oficina de Arquitectura
text:
Biarritz Building - Cooperative Housing / Ariel Jacubovich | Oficina de Arquitectura

Biarritz is a 35-unit residential building in the district of San Martín, Province of Buenos Aires, developed alongside a cooperative of teachers and education workers. It is the result of a participatory process initiated in 2017 that spanned from searching for the land to the actual construction, including training workshops, debates on ways of living, and even policy proposals for democratic housing development created in collaboration with local organizations.
